text: You signed up for a gym membership, hoping to get fit and use the equipment whenever you want for a reasonable price.
But sometimes, you arrive to find it completely packed, with every machine occupied and long waits for free weights.
You might wonder how they can possibly sustain a business if it's always this full, or why they sold so many spots.
The invisible system is simple: most members pay but rarely show up, meaning the gym's actual capacity is rarely tested.
Your affordable membership is only possible because the thousands who pay and don't come subsidize the few who train regularly.
Now, when you see a crowded gym, you understand it's not oversold, but perfectly balanced by the unseen majority.
